Hi Samir —

Thanks again for the demo this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a single plan for the POC and the observability work your team requested.

Summary from today
- Goal: Validate Redwood Dedicated for CloudDesk search assistant (latency under 200ms p95, sustained throughput ~40 tokens/sec per session) and ensure observability meets SRE requirements for production cutover.
- Scope for trial: 2-week trial on Dedicated with a 3k token/session synthetic workload + 24/7 trace & metrics export to your Splunk instance.

Proposed success criteria (short):
1) Latency: p95 <= 200ms for 90% of test sessions
2) Error budget: < 0.5% client-visible errors during test window
3) Telemetry: request-level traces + token-level counters exported and searchable in Splunk within 5 minutes
4) Cost baseline: tokens/second and GPU-hour metrics reported to your billing dashboard

Immediate asks / next steps
- We (Redwood) will provision a Dedicated trial cluster and share access by Wed EOD (Oct 7).
- CloudDesk to confirm support contact for Splunk ingestion and provide a test index/endpoint by Tue (Oct 6).
- Jordan will own observability dashboard setup; Jonas will own the quality/eval scripts and load harness.

Attachments: POC_Success_Criteria.xlsx (outline + KPI matrix) and observability-dashboard-template.png (wireframe) attached.

If that looks right I'll lock in the timeline and send a short mutual action plan doc.

Best,

Hi Samir — great; thanks for the fast reply. I’ll own Splunk ingestion and the dashboard. A few specifics I’ll implement for the POC: 

- Traces: request_id propagated; full span for model tokenization -> generation -> post-processing. Traces exported to Splunk APM via OpenTelemetry.
- Metrics (exported to your HEC endpoint):
  * redwood.requests.total (counter, tags: model, environment)
  * redwood.requests.errors (counter, tags: error_type)
  * redwood.latency.p50/p95/p99 (histogram)
  * redwood.kv_cache.hit_ratio (gauge)
  * redwood.token_rate (gauge; tokens/sec per instance)
- Logs: structured JSON logs with request_id, user_id (hashed), model_version, and reason codes; log export to your index with 5-minute batching.
- Dashboards: I’ll deploy a starter dashboard with 6 panels — latency distribution, error rate, throughput, KV cache hit%, token-level churn, and trace waterfall for slow requests.
- Alerts: implement a Splunk alert rule for error rate > 0.3% over 15m that posts to your Slack channel; also p95 latency spike > 400ms for 10m.

I’ll need the HEC token + index name and a test Slack webhook for alert posting. I’ll stand up the dashboard on our side and share a link for you to import.

-Jordan
